# Joint Application 32855 — Backlog Closeout vs. Merits Review

## Bottom line
Application **32855 was not decided on its merits.** It was swept up in a single
backlog closeout on **2025-04-09** that bulk-rejected long-stuck joint applications.
In the June-2024 cohort around 32855, **50 of 115** applications were disposed of on
that one day — every one of them rejected — after sitting in manual review for
~9–10 months. Critically, the closeout closed the *account* applications while leaving
most of the underlying person KYC checks un-adjudicated: **68 of 100** applicants in the
swept set were still in `manual_review` when their application was rejected, and
**18 of the 50** swept applications had **both** applicants still stuck.

## Method
All figures come from the `zeta3` warehouse (catalog `zeta3`, schema `rds`), not from
policy pages. Source tables:
- `account_applications` — the account-level application (status, `original_status`,
  `manual_review_mailers_sent_at`, `final_decisioned_at`, `account_type`).
- `account_person_applications` — join table (`person_application_id` ↔ `account_application_id`).
- `person_applications` — per-applicant record carrying `kyc_status` / `initial_kyc_status` /
  `kyced_at`.
- `kyc_data` — the KYC vendor outcome (`outcome`, `outcome_reasons`, `processed_at`) keyed to a
  person application.

**Cohort definition.** "Went into manual review around the same time as 32855 (opened
early June 2024)" = joint (`account_type='joint'`) account applications whose
`manual_review_mailers_sent_at` fell in **June 2024** (`[2024-06-01, 2024-07-01)`).
Every one of these 115 also carries `original_status='manual_review'`, confirming they
all genuinely entered manual review (this is the entry signal; `manual_review_mailers_sent_at`
is the entry timestamp).

**Sweep detection.** For the cohort, the time from manual-review entry to final decision is
strongly bimodal: a merits cluster at 0–28 days, and a long-stuck cluster at 283–312 days.
Grouping the cohort's `final_decisioned_at` by day shows a single dominant spike —
**2025-04-09, 50 applications** — and that spike is exactly the long-stuck cluster. No other
day comes close (next largest day is 19, a normal ~2–3 week review batch in June, not a
closeout). I therefore classify each cohort member into one bucket:
- **aged_out** — `final_decisioned_at` on 2025-04-09 (the backlog closeout).
- **resolved_before_sweep** — decided on its own merits before 2025-04-09.
- **still_manual_review** — no `final_decisioned_at` (still open, status `manual_review`).

**Applicant-level trace.** For the 50 aged-out applications I joined to
`account_person_applications` → `person_applications` (100 applicants, 2 per app). An
applicant's KYC is "unresolved" when `kyc_status='manual_review'` (never moved to a
terminal `approved`/`denied`).

**Robustness check.** The same 2025-04-09 spike hits the neighbouring entry months too
(joint apps that entered manual review in May 2024: 50 swept; July 2024: 103 swept —
203 total on that day). So 2025-04-09 was a single platform-wide closeout event, not an
artifact of the June window.

## Cohort finding (joint apps entering manual review, June 2024)

| Bucket | Count | Status detail |
|---|---|---|
| **aged_out** (swept 2025-04-09) | **50** | all `rejected` |
| resolved_before_sweep (merits) | 64 | 42 `approved` + 22 `rejected` |
| still_manual_review (open, no decision) | 1 | app 33001 (entered MR 2024-06-21) |
| **cohort_size** | **115** | all `original_status='manual_review'` |

- 50 + 64 + 1 = 115 ✓
- Time-to-decision: merits group resolved in 0–28 days (median ~1–3 days); swept group
  stuck 283–312 days, then all rejected on 2025-04-09.
- The merits group was approved 66% of the time (42/64); the swept group was rejected
  100% of the time (50/50) — the closeout was a "reject the backlog" action, not case-by-case adjudication.

### Applicant level — for the 50 swept applications (100 applicants)
- **unresolved_person_kyc = 68** — applicants whose `kyc_status` is still `manual_review`
  (KYC never moved out of manual review).
- 32 applicants did resolve to `approved`; 0 to `denied`; none null/pending/invalidated.
- **both_applicants_unresolved = 18** — applications where *both* applicants were still stuck
  in `manual_review` at closeout.
- The remaining 32 swept applications had one applicant unresolved and one approved.

(Consistency: 18 apps × 2 stuck + 32 apps × 1 stuck = 68 unresolved; 18 + 32 = 50 apps.)

## 32855 walkthrough (the example)
- Account application **32855**: `account_type='joint'`, `application_type='standard'`,
  product `personal_checking`, `kyc_model='zeta_journey_v1'`.
- **Opened** `created_at = 2024-06-04 03:39`; entered manual review the same minute
  (`manual_review_mailers_sent_at = 2024-06-04 03:41`; `original_status='manual_review'`).
- **Final decision** `final_decisioned_at = 2025-04-09 16:56`, terminal `status='rejected'`.
- **Days in manual review = 309** (`date_diff('day', manual_review_mailers_sent_at, final_decisioned_at)`; same as days since open).
- 32855 is one of the 50 swept apps and one of the 18 both-applicants-unresolved apps.

Linked applicants (via `account_person_applications` → `person_applications`):

| Person app | User | `initial_kyc_status` | `kyc_status` (now) | KYC vendor `outcome` / `outcome_reasons` | `processed_at` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80596 | 106471 | manual_review | **manual_review** (unresolved) | "Manual Review" / {Fraud Review} | 2024-06-04 03:39 |
| 80597 | 106472 | manual_review | **manual_review** (unresolved) | "Manual Review" / {Fraud Review, Denied KYC, Name Not Verified, SSN Not Verified} | 2024-06-04 03:39 |

Both `person_applications` rows still show `kyc_status='manual_review'` — neither person's
KYC was ever adjudicated. The account was nonetheless rejected 10 months later on the
sweep date. So the "terminal status the member does not understand" (`rejected`) was the
backlog closeout, not a merits determination on either applicant.

## Recommendation
1. **Treat 32855 as a backlog-closeout rejection, not a KYC denial.** Reopen/allow re-submission
   without prejudice — neither applicant was ever adjudicated, and one (80596) had only a
   single "Fraud Review" flag with no substantive denial reasons.
2. **Bulk-remediate the other 17 "both-unresolved" swept applications** (18 total incl. 32855):
   these were rejected on 2025-04-09 while both applicants' KYC sat in `manual_review`. At
   minimum, notify these members that the rejection was administrative, not substantive, and
   offer re-application. Consider the same for the 32 "one-unresolved" swept apps where one
   applicant's KYC was never resolved.
3. **Audit the closeout process.** A single-day rejection of 203 long-stuck joint
   applications (May–July 2024 entrants), 100% rejected and 68% with unresolved person KYC,
   looks like a queue-age-out rather than review. Recommend a guardrail that prevents
   `account_applications` from being decisioned to `rejected` while linked
   `person_applications.kyc_status` remains `manual_review`, and add SLA/aging alerts before
   applications hit ~300 days in manual review.
4. **Track the one still-open case** (app 33001, in manual review since 2024-06-21) so it is
   not silently re-swept in a future closeout.
